newsitem.title: INDIA: Fire guts domestic airport terminal in New Delhi.
newsitem.headline: Fire guts domestic airport terminal in New Delhi.

text.p: Fire destroyed the main departure terminal for domestic Indian Airlines flights at New Delhi's airport on Wednesday but no injuries were reported, airport officials said.
The blaze erupted at 0330 a.m. (2200 GMT Tuesday) and debris was still smouldering seven hours later. The terminal was gutted.
"The fire was ferocious. It will take at least four months to reconstruct the terminal," Harbans Kumar, the airport director, told Reuters at the scene.
Flight services were disrupted for three hours but resumed later from an adjacent terminal for private domestic airlines, officials said.

The airport's international terminal is located in the same large area as the domestic terminals and was not affected by the fire, although airport officials said 10 international flights were diverted in the morning.
An official in charge of airport operations, Roby Lal, said the fire broke out in the restaurant of the Indian Airlines terminal. The cause was not immediately known.
By mid-morning, black soot covered much of the remains of the single-storey building built on New Delhi's outskirts in 1982.
Kumar said he saw the fire shortly after it broke out and that flames rose to a height of more than 30 feet (9.2 metres).
Flames quickly engulfed the terminal. More than 50 fire-fighters in 10 vehicles reached the scene minutes after the blaze started, he added.
Airport officials had to call for a further 32 fire trucks from the city.
The terminal, for all flights operated by state-owned Indian Airlines, handled more than 20,000 passengers daily.
Air-India is the country's international airline.
